focused_test_modules.covers: anchored pathspec matching, character classes and escapes, path normalisation refusals, glob intersection with witness verification, a brute-force property cross-check, and a differential comparison against git's own ':(glob)' engine

static overlap against preregistered pairs, registry/task-input divergence, advisory findings, admission of the fixture change sets, rename and delete sides, fence and writer rules, 'git --name-status -z' parsing, document validation and CLI exit codes

traversal, absolute and drive-letter paths, doubled and backslash separators, quoted and control-character paths, case variants, decomposed Unicode, glob metacharacters appearing in data, deny precedence over a grant of '**', implicit deny survival, fence evasion, owner-id case evasion, unrecognised statuses, report serialisation and scale

each step of the sanitized pre-commit reproduction, including that HEAD does not move and the owner's committed bytes survive a refused overwrite, and that the negative control commits when the gate is bypassed

the read-back manifest path label, the twelve cross-field agreement checks and the seven narrative-figure checks, each stale-figure and mislabel case that occurred on this branch, and the committed return document itself

fixture_coverage.detail: 8 colliding glob pairs across exactly the 8 preregistered owner pairs; every witness verified against both grants
16 deliberately prohibited writes, each denied for its preregistered reason code
10 cases with preregistered per-side reason codes, mixing admitted and refused sides
15 crafted paths, each denied for its preregistered reason, none silently rewritten into an admitted path

reproduction.enforcement_point: git pre-commit hook invoking the engine on the staged index
reproduction.external_effects: none: temporary local repository, no network, no secrets

post_return_run.why: result/ready-to-commit.json is written after the manifest is hashed, so the artifact captured in test-output.txt cannot include the run that reads it. That run is reported here and re-executed from a clean clone of the return commit.
post_return_run.recorded_in: the producer terminal response, alongside the clean-clone reproduction of the return commit

clean_runtime_reproducibility.note: tests/test_gitglob.py and tests/test_prevention_reproduction.py skip if git is absent rather than failing; both ran here.
